SURAH HUD

(p-72) Its revelation

Ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas that it is entirely Meccan. This was also the view of al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Jabir ibn Zayd and Qatadah. It is also related from Ibn Abbas that he said: "It is Meccan, except for one verse, which is His saying: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day﴾ [Hud: 114]." Qatadah said the same. Muqatil said: "It is entirely Meccan, except His saying: ﴿So perhaps you will leave aside part of what is revealed to you﴾ [Hud: 12], His saying: ﴿Those believe in it﴾ [Hud: 17], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ [Hud: 114]."

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that he said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, gray hair has come upon you early.' He said: 'Hud and its sister surahs have made me gray: al-Haqqah, al-Waqi'ah, ʿAmma yatasaʾalun, and Hal ataka hadith al-ghashiyah.'"

(p-73) As for "Alif Lam Ra", we have already mentioned its explanation in the surah of Yunus.

Al-Farra' said: "And 'Kitab' is in the nominative case, governed by the disjointed letters preceding it, as if you said: 'The letters of the alphabet are this Qur'an.' If you wish, you may put it in the nominative by supposing 'This is a Book' (implied)." The Kitab here means the Qur'an.

Regarding His saying ﴿its verses were made firm﴾ there are four opinions:

One: they were made firm, so they are not abrogated by another book as earlier books and laws were abrogated. This was said by Ibn Abbas and chosen by Ibn Qutaybah.

The second: they were made firm by command and prohibition. This was said by al-Hasan and Abu al-ʿAliyah.

The third: they were made firm against falsehood, meaning they were protected. This was said by Qatadah and Muqatil.

The fourth: "made firm" means "gathered together." This was said by Ibn Zayd.

If it is asked: how did He make the verses general in firmness here, while in His saying ﴿In it are muhkam verses﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7] He specified some of them? There are two answers.

One is that the firmness mentioned here in general is other than the firmness specified there.

As for the general meaning of firmness, there are five opinions, four of which we have already stated in His saying "its verses were made firm." The fifth is that it is the inimitability of the composition and eloquence, and the inclusion of wise judgments that cannot be matched.

(p-74) The specific meaning of firmness is the removal of ambiguity and the equal understanding of the meaning of the verse among listeners.

The second answer is that firmness in both places has one meaning. The meaning of His saying "its verses were made firm" is that some of them were made firm through clear explanation and the prevention of ambiguity, so the general was used to mean the specific, as the Arabs say: "I have eaten the food of Zayd," meaning some of his food; and they say: "We were killed, by the Lord of the Ka'bah," meaning some of us were killed. Ibn al-Anbari mentioned this.

Regarding His saying "then it was detailed" there are six opinions:

One: it was detailed with the lawful and the unlawful. This was narrated by Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas.

The second: it was detailed with reward and punishment. This was narrated by Jisr ibn Farqad from al-Hasan.

The third: it was detailed with promise and warning. This was narrated by Abu Bakr al-Hudhali from al-Hasan as well.

The fourth: "detailed" means "explained." This was said by Mujahid.

The fifth: it was sent down piece by piece, not all at once. Ibn Qutaybah mentioned this.

The sixth: it was detailed with everything needed of proof for the Oneness of God, the confirmation of the prophethood of the prophets, and the establishment of laws. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿from One who is All-Wise, All-Aware﴾ means: from His presence.

(p-75) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That you worship none but Allah﴾. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is: "Its verses have been made distinct, [in the sense] that you worship none but Allah, and [that] ﴿seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾." The word "*anna*" (that) is in the accusative position, by dropping the preposition (*khafd*, the removal of the governing particle).

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: "I command you that you worship none [but Allah], and that you seek forgiveness."

Muqatil said: The intended meaning of this worship is monotheism (*tawhid*). The address is to the disbelievers of Makkah.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance﴾. On this there are two views:

The first: that the seeking of forgiveness and repentance here are from shirk (associating partners with Allah). This was said by Muqatil.

The second: "Seek forgiveness from Him for past sins, then turn to Him in repentance from future sins whenever they occur." It is reported from al-Farra' that he said: "*Thumma*" (then) here has the meaning of *wa* (and).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He will let you enjoy a good provision﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He will bestow upon you sustenance and abundance. Ibn Qutaybah said: He will let you live long. The root of *al-imta'* (enjoyment) is lengthening [of time]. It is said: "Allah has lengthened [your life] through you" (*amta'a Allahu bika*) and "Allah has made you enjoy [life] through you" (*matta'a Allahu bika*), *imta'an* and *mata'an*. A long thing is called *mati'*: one says "a long mountain" (*jabal mati'*), and "the day has lengthened" (*mata'a al-nahar*) when it has extended.

Regarding the meaning of ﴿the appointed term﴾, there are two views:

The first: that it is death. This was said by Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, and by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The second: that it is the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And He will give every person of merit his merit﴾. Concerning the pronoun (*ha' al-kinayah*, the pronominal suffix) there are two views:

The first: that it refers back to Allah, the Exalted. Then, concerning the meaning of the statement, there are two views: One: "And He will give every person of merit, of good deeds, the best of His bounty, which is Paradise." The second: "He will give him His bounty of guidance to righteous deeds."

The second: that it refers back to the servant, so the meaning is: "And He will give everyone who increases in his goodness (p-76) and acts of obedience the reward of that increase which he has added, so He will favour him in this world with a high station, and in the Hereafter with a great reward."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But if you turn away﴾, that is: if you turn away from what you have been commanded. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Mijlaz, and Abu Raja' read *wa-in tuwallu* with a *damma* on the *ta'* (i.e., *tuwallu*, in the passive form). ﴿Indeed I fear for you﴾: here there is an elided *fa-qul* (so say), understood by implication. The "great day" is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verse 5:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, they fold their chests﴾. Concerning the occasion of its revelation there are five opinions:

The first: it was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who used to sit with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and swear that he loved him, while concealing the opposite of what he showed him. So this verse was revealed concerning him. Abu Salih narrated it from Ibn Abbas.

The second: it was revealed concerning people who were ashamed to relieve themselves in the open under the sky and to have intercourse with their wives, so this verse was revealed concerning them. Muhammad ibn Abbad narrated it from Ibn Abbas.

The third: it was revealed concerning some of the hypocrites who, when they passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), would bend their chest and back, lower their heads, and cover their faces so that the Messenger of Allah would not see them. Abdullah ibn Shaddad said this.

The fourth: a group of the polytheists said: "When we close our doors, let down our curtains, cover ourselves with our garments, and fold our chests over our enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ), how would he know about us?" So Allah informed them of what they concealed. Al-Zajjaj mentioned it.

The fifth: it was revealed concerning a people who, because of the intensity of their enmity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when they heard the Qur'an from him, would bow their chests, lower their heads, and wrap their garments around themselves so that the voice of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would be far from them and nothing of the Qur'an would enter their ears. Ibn al-Anbari mentioned it.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿they fold their chests﴾. It is said: "I folded the thing" when you bent it and wrapped it. Regarding the meaning of the words there are five opinions:

The first: they conceal what is in them of enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ). Abu Salih narrated it from Ibn Abbas.

The second: they fold their chests over disbelief. Mujahid said this.

The third: they bend them so that they do not hear the Book of Allah. Qatadah said this.

The fourth: they fold them when some of them confer privately with one another about the matter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ibn Zayd said this.

The fifth: they fold them out of shame before Allah, the Exalted, and this comes out according to what we related from Ibn Abbas. Ibn al-Anbari said: Ibn Abbas used to read it as "Alla innahum tathnawi sudurahum" ("Indeed, their chests fold"), and he explained it as meaning that people were ashamed to relieve themselves in the open under the sky and to have intercourse with their wives. So "tathnawi" is on the pattern "taf'awil," and it is a verb for the chests, meaning: exaggeration in the folding of the chests, just as the Arabs say: "ihlawla al-shay'," "yahlawli," when they exaggerate in describing it as sweet. Antarah said:

Unquestioned, may Allah curse the ruined encampments,
and may Allah curse the remembrance of the bygone years.
***
And your saying to the thing you cannot reach,
when it becomes sweet: "Would that this were mine!"

According to this view, the verse concerns the believers, and according to the rest of the opinions, it concerns the hypocrites. From these opinions regarding the meaning of ﴿they fold their chests﴾ come two statements: the first, that it is literal, concerning the chests; the second, that it is concealment of what is in them.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿that they may hide from Him﴾. Regarding the pronoun in "minhu" ("from Him") there are two opinions: the first, that it refers to Allah, the Exalted; the second, that it refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments﴾. Abu Ubaydah said: the Arabs use "ala" for emphasis, affirmation, and alerting. Ibn Qutaybah said: ﴿they cover themselves with their garments﴾ means they wrap themselves in them and conceal themselves with them. Qatadah said: the son of Adam is most hidden when he bends his back, covers himself with his garment, and conceals his concern within himself. Ibn al-Anbari said: Allah informed that He knows their inner secrets just as He knows what they display.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the chests﴾. We have explained it in (Al 'Imran: 119).

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verses 6–7:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: "min" (مِن) is among the particles of addition (ḥurūf al-zawā'id), and the meaning is: "and there is no creature." The word dābba (دابَّة) is a name for every living thing that crawls. His saying: ﴿but upon Allah is its provision﴾. The scholars said: this is out of His bounty, not as an obligation upon Him. Here "upon" (عَلى) is in the sense of "from" (مِن). We have already mentioned the distinction between "al-mustaqarr" (the permanent abode) and "al-mustawda'" (the temporary repository) in Surah al-An'am (6:67).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿All is in a Book﴾. That is, this is with Allah in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). This is the saying of the exegetes. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that this is established in the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And His Throne was upon the water﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "His Throne" means His seat (sarir), and the water, when the Throne was upon it, was upon the wind. Qatada said: that was before He created the heavens and the earth.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That He may test you﴾. That is, that He may test you with the test by which He recompenses, so He rewards the one who takes heed by what he sees of the signs of the heavens and the earth, and punishes the people of obstinacy.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Which of you is best in deed﴾. Regarding this there are four sayings: First, "Which of you has the best intellect, is most scrupulous regarding the prohibitions of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and is swiftest in obedience to Allah." Ibn 'Umar narrated it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The second: "Which of you is most active in obedience to Allah," said by Ibn 'Abbas. The third: "Which of you is most complete in intellect," said by Qatada. The fourth: "Which of you is most ascetic regarding the world," said by al-Hasan and Sufyan.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿This is nothing but evident magic﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: magic is falsehood in their view, so it is as if they said: "This is nothing but evident falsehood." So Allah, Exalted is He, informed them that the power to create the heavens and the earth indicates the resurrection of the dead.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verse 8:

(p-80) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them﴾. The exegetes said: These are the disbelievers of Makkah. By "the countable nation" (al-ummah al-ma'dudah) is meant the known term (al-ajal al-ma'lum), and the meaning is: until the coming of one nation and the extinction of another before it. ﴿They will surely say, "What is holding it back?"﴾ They only said this as denial and mockery.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them﴾, and He said: ﴿it will not be averted from them﴾. Some said: The punishment will not be turned away from them when it comes upon them. Others said: When the swords of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seize them, they will not be sheathed from them until the people of disbelief are annihilated and the word of sincere monotheism (kalimat al-ikhlas) prevails.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and what they used to mock encompassed them﴾. Abu 'Ubaydah said: It descended upon them and befell them.

Regarding His saying: ﴿what they used to mock﴾, there are two opinions. The first: it refers to the Messenger and the Book; this was said by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas. The meaning then is: the recompense of their mockery encompassed them. The second: it refers to the punishment; they used to mock by saying, "What is holding it back?" This is the view of Muqatil.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verse 9:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us﴾, the scholars differed concerning whom it was revealed about, in three opinions:

The first: that it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira; this was said by Ibn Abbas. The second: concerning Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya al-Makhzumi; this was mentioned by al-Wahidi (al-Wahidi). The third: that "man" (al-insan) here is a generic noun (ism jins), and the meaning is: "And if We let people taste..."; this was said by al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj).

The intended meaning of "mercy" (al-rahma) is blessing (al-ni'ma), such as good health (al-afiya), wealth (al-mal), and children (al-walad).

And "yaʼus" (al-yaʼus) means despair (al-qunut). Abu Ubayda said: it is fa'ul (fa'ul), from "ya'istu" (I despaired). Muqatil said: "Indeed, he is despairing (la-ya'us) at the time of hardship, regarding good, ungrateful (kafur) to Allah for His blessings in times of ease."

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verse 10:

Allah's words, ﴿And if We let him taste a favor⁠﻿ after hardship had touched him﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Health and abundance in provision." ﴿After hardship had touched him﴾: after sickness and poverty. ﴿He will surely say, "The evils have gone away from me"﴾: meaning the harm and poverty. ﴿Indeed, he is exultant⁠﻿ and boastful﴾: that is, insolent (baṭar). ﴿Boastful﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said, "He boasts before My friends of what I have made abundant for him."

If it is asked: What is the reason for finding fault with the human being in his saying, ﴿The evils have gone away from me﴾, and what is the reason for blaming him for exultation, when Allah described the martyrs, saying, "fariheen" (rejoicing)?

Ibn al-Anbari has answered this. He said: He found fault with him through his saying, ﴿The evils have gone away from me﴾, because he did not acknowledge Allah's blessing and did not praise Him for what was turned away from him. He blamed him for this exultation because it refers to the meaning of arrogance (maraḥ) and pride (takabbur) in opposition to obedience to Allah. The poet said:

"The vicissitudes of time do not make me forget my honor,
nor do I cast off my waist-wrap out of exultation (faraḥ)."

He means out of arrogance (maraḥ). The exultation of the martyrs is an exultation without pride or conceit; rather, it is accompanied by gratitude, so it is praiseworthy.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verse 11:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except those who are patient﴾. Al-Farra' said: this exception is from "man" (al-insan), because it carries the sense of "people" (al-nas), like His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ ﴿except those who have believed﴾ [al-'Asr: 2, 3]. Al-Zajjaj said: this is an exception that is not from the first (group), and the meaning is: "But those who are patient." Ibn 'Abbas said: the first description is for the disbeliever, and "those who are patient" are the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verse 12:

(p-82) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Perhaps you would leave out some of what is revealed to you﴾. The occasion of its revelation was that the disbelievers of Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it﴾ [Yunus: 15]. The Prophet (ﷺ) then resolved not to let them hear the defects of their gods, hoping that they would follow him, so this verse was revealed. This was related by Muqatil. There are two opinions regarding the meaning of the verse:

One: Perhaps you would leave out conveying some of what is revealed to you concerning the matter of the gods, and your breast would be constricted by what you have been charged with in this regard, out of fear that they would say: ﴿Why has a treasure not been sent down to him?﴾

The second: Perhaps, because of the great weight that the confusion they create falls upon your heart, you would imagine that they might turn you away from some part of what you hold of your Lord's command.

As for "ḍā'iq" (constricted), it has the meaning of "ḍayq" (narrowness). Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of "an yaqūlū" (that they should say) is "karāhiyat an yaqūlū" (out of aversion that they should say). Your only duty is to warn them with what is revealed to you; it is not incumbent upon you to bring them the signs they propose.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah is Guardian over all things﴾. Regarding it there are two opinions: One: that He is the Guardian (al-Ḥāfiẓ). The second: the Witness (al-Shahīd). We have mentioned it in (Al 'Imran: 173).

The commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 11, verses 13–14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ "Am" (أم) here has the meaning of "bal" (بل, "rather"), and "iftarahu" (افتراه) means that he brought it from himself. "Say: Then bring" — you, in opposing me — ﴿ten surahs like it﴾ in eloquence (p-83) ﴿invented﴾ according to your claim and assertion, ﴿and call upon whomever you can besides Allah﴾ for help in the counter-challenge (mu'aradah, "opposition" or matching the Qur'an), ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your saying, "He has invented it."

﴿And if they do not respond to you﴾, that is, if they do not answer you with the counter-challenge, then the proof has been established against them in your favour.

If it is asked: how did He use the singular in His saying, ﴿Say: then bring﴾, and then the plural in His saying, ﴿if they do not respond to you﴾? There are two answers to this. The first: the address is to the Prophet ﷺ alone in both places, and the address to him with "lakum" (لكم, "you," plural) is an honour, because addressing one person with the plural form is a mark of respect. This is the view of the exegetes (mufassirun). The second: He used the singular in the first place because the address is to the Prophet ﷺ, and the plural in the second because the address is to the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. This was said by Ibn al-Anbari.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So know that it was sent down with the knowledge of Allah﴾. Regarding this there are two views. The first: He sent it down while knowing that He was sending it down, and knowing that it is the truth from Him. The second: He sent it down with what it informs of the unseen (al-ghayb), and it indicates what will happen and what has passed. Al-Zajjaj mentioned both views.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that there is no god but Him﴾, that is, know this. ﴿Will you then submit?﴾ This is a question with the meaning of a command. Regarding who is addressed by it there are two views. The first: the people of Makkah, and their submission (islam) means sincerely devoting worship to Allah; this was said by Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas. The second: that they are the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; this was said by Mujahid.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verses 15–16:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾. The scholars of tafsir (exegesis) differed about whom this verse was revealed concerning, in four opinions:

The first: it is general, encompassing all of creation, and this is the view of the majority.

The second: it concerns the people of the qiblah (the Muslims), as related by Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas.

The third: it concerns the Jews and Christians, as stated by Anas.

The fourth: it concerns the people of showing off (riya'), as stated by Mujahid.

And ʿAtaʾ related from Ibn Abbas: "Whoever desires the immediate (benefit of) this world and does not believe in the Resurrection and recompense." Others said: it refers only to the disbeliever, because the believer desires both this world and the Hereafter.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We will pay them in full for their deeds﴾, meaning: the rewards of their deeds ﴿therein﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are given the reward for whatever good they did in this world. Mujahid said: whoever performs a deed of kinship or charity without seeking the Face of Allah, Allah gives him the reward for that in this world, and He wards off harm from him in this world by means of it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they therein﴾. Ibn Abbas said: meaning, in this world. ﴿Will not be deprived﴾, meaning: they will not have anything of their deeds diminished in this world. ﴿Those are the ones who﴾ did deeds for other than Allah, ﴿for them in the Hereafter there is nothing but the Fire, and what they did will be nullified﴾, meaning: what they did in this world of good ﴿and vain is what they used to do﴾ for other than Allah.

Section

Some of the mufassirun, including Muqatil, mentioned that this verse implies that whoever desires the world by his deed is given therein the reward of his deed in provision and good, and then this was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: ﴿We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We intend﴾ [al-Isra' 17:18]. But this is not sound, because He only pays in full to those whom He intends.

(p-85) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is one who has a clear proof (bayyinah) from his Lord﴾. Regarding the meaning of bayyinah (clear proof) there are four opinions:

The first is that it is the religion (al-din). This was said by Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas. The second is that it is the Messenger of God (ﷺ). This was said by al-Dahhak. The third is the Qur'an. This was said by Ibn Zayd. The fourth is the clarification (al-bayan). This was said by Muqatil.

As for what is referred to by "min" (from): there are two opinions. The first is that it is the Messenger of God (ﷺ). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and the majority. The second is that they are the Muslims, and this can be derived from the view of al-Dahhak.

Regarding His saying, ﴿and a witness recites it﴾ (wa yatluhu): there are two opinions. The first is that it means "follows it." The second is that it means "recites it."

Regarding the pronoun in yatluhu (the "hu"): there are two opinions. The first is that it refers to the Prophet (ﷺ). The second is that it refers to the Qur'an, which was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿Then bring ten surahs like it, forged﴾ [Hud 11:13].

Regarding what is meant by the witness (shahid), there are eight opinions:

The first is that it is Jibril (Gabriel). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ibrahim, and others.

The second is that it is the tongue of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) which recited the Qur'an. This was said by Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others.

(p-86) The third is that it is Ali ibn Abi Talib. Here yatluhu means "follows it." A group narrated this from Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Muhammad ibn Ali and Zayd ibn Ali also said this.

The fourth is that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) himself is a witness from God, the Exalted. This was said by al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).

The fifth is that it is an angel who protects and guides him. This was said by Mujahid.

The sixth is that it is the Gospel (al-Injil), which recites the Qur'an by confirming it, even though it was revealed before it, because the Torah gave glad tidings of the Prophet (ﷺ). This was said by al-Farra'.

The seventh is that it is the Qur'an itself, its arrangement and its inimitability (i'jaz). This was said by al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl.

The eighth is that it is the form, face and features of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), because every intelligent person who looked at him knew that he was the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Regarding the pronoun in minhu (the "hu" in "from him"), there are three opinions. The first is that it refers to God, the Exalted. The second is that it refers to the Prophet (ﷺ). The third is that it refers to the bayyinah.

His saying, ﴿and before it﴾ (wa min qablihi): regarding this pronoun there are three opinions. The first is that it refers to the Prophet (ﷺ). This was said by Mujahid. The second is that it refers to the Qur'an. This was said by Ibn Zayd. The third is that it refers to the Gospel, meaning: and before the Gospel was ﴿the Book of Musa﴾ (kitab Musa), confirming Muhammad (ﷺ) by affirming him. This was mentioned by Ibn al-Anbari.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that before this there was the Book of Musa as a guide to the matter of the Prophet (ﷺ). So ﴿the Book of Musa﴾ is coordinated (atf) with His saying: ﴿and a witness recites it from Him﴾, meaning: and the Book of Musa recites it, because Musa and Isa gave glad tidings of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Torah and the Gospel. The word imaman (as a leader) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal).

If it is said: how can the Torah "recite" it when it came before it?

(p-87) It is said: when it gave glad tidings of him, it was as if it were reciting him, because it followed him by confirming him.

Ibn al-Anbari said: ﴿the Book of Musa﴾ is in meaning an object (maf'ul), because Jibril recited it to Musa, so the Book was raised (in case). It is the object of an implied verb after it, its interpretation being: and before it there was the Book of Musa likewise, meaning Jibril also recited it, just as the Arabs say: "I honored your brother and your father," raising "the father," and he is honored by way of resumption (istinaf), meaning: "and your father is honored too." He said: a group went to the view that the Book of Musa is the subject (fa'il), because it recited Muhammad (ﷺ) by confirmation, just as the Gospel recited him.

Section

The summary of the verse is: Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord like one who does not? Al-Zajjaj said: the opposite was omitted, because what follows contains evidence of it, which is His saying: ﴿The likeness of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf﴾ [Hud 11:24]. Ibn Qutaybah said: when He mentioned before this verse a people who inclined to the world, He brought this verse, and the sense of the speech is: Is one whose state is this like one who desires the world? He was content with the answer from what preceded, since it contained evidence of it. Ibn al-Anbari said: it was omitted because the meaning is clear, and the implied omitted element is frequent in the Qur'an and in poetry. A poet said:

"Then I swear, if any thing had come to us from his messenger, other than you, but we did not find for you any repelling."

If we say that what is meant by "one who has a clear proof from his Lord" is the Messenger of God (ﷺ), then the meaning of the verse is: a witness follows this Prophet, and it is Jibril (peace be upon him). "From him" means from God. It was also said: the witness is Ali ibn Abi Talib, and "from him" means from the Prophet (ﷺ). It was also said: "recites it" means the Qur'an, which Jibril recites, and he is a witness for Muhammad (ﷺ) that what he recites came from God, the Exalted. It was also said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recites the Qur'an, and he is a witness from God. It was also said: the tongue of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recites the Qur'an, so his tongue is a witness from him. It was also said: a witness confirming Muhammad (ﷺ) follows him, and it is the Gospel from God, the Exalted. It was also said: a witness from himself follows this Prophet, and it is his character and his guidance, which indicate his truthfulness.

If we say that what is meant by "one who has a clear proof from his Lord" is the Muslims, then the meaning is: they follow the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who is the clear proof, and a witness to his truthfulness follows this Prophet.

His saying, ﴿as a leader and a mercy﴾ (imaman wa rahmah): he was called an imam only because he was guided by it. "And a mercy" means "and possessing mercy." He meant by this the Torah, because it was a leader and a cause of mercy for whoever believed in it.

His saying, ﴿those﴾ (ula'ika): regarding it there are three opinions. The first is that it refers to the companions of Musa. The second is that it refers to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). The third is that it refers to the people of truth from the nations of Musa, Isa and Muhammad.

Regarding the pronoun in bihi (the "hi" in "in it"), there are three opinions. The first is that it refers to the Torah. The second is that it refers to the Qur'an. The third is that it refers to Muhammad (ﷺ).

Regarding what is meant by "the factions" (al-ahzab) here, there are four opinions: The first is all the religious communities. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. The second is the Jews and the Christians. This was said by Qatadah. The third is Quraysh. This was said by al-Suddi. The fourth is the Banu Umayyah, the Banu al-Mughirah ibn Abd Allah al-Makhzumi, and the family of Abu Talhah ibn Abd al-Uzza. This was said by Muqatil.

(p-89) His saying, ﴿So the Fire is his promised place﴾ (fa'l-naru mawiduhu): meaning, his destination is toward it. Hassan ibn Thabit said:

"You brought them to the watering-places of death in the open, so the Fire is their appointed place, and death meets them."

His saying, ﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾ (fa-la taku fi miryatin minhu): Al-Hasan and Qatadah read "muryah" with a dhammah on the mim wherever it occurs. Regarding what the pronoun refers to, there are two opinions:

The first is that it is the report of the disbelievers' destination because of it, so the meaning is: do not be in doubt that the promised place of those who deny it is the Fire. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second is that it is the Qur'an, so the meaning is: do not be in doubt that the Qur'an is from God, the Exalted. This was said by Muqatil. Ibn 'Abbas said: what is meant by "the people" here is the people of Makkah.

His saying, ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord﴾: Al-Zajjaj said: He mentioned their being presented in order to emphasize their state regarding retribution against them, even though others are also presented.

As for "the witnesses" (al-ashhad), there are five opinions regarding them: The first is that they are the messengers. This was said by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas. The second is the angels. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah. The third is the creatures; this was also narrated from Qatadah. Muqatil said: "al-ashhad" means the people, as one says "in the presence of the witnesses," meaning in the presence of the people. The fourth is the angels, the prophets, and the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), who bear witness over the people, and the limbs bear witness against the son of Adam. This was said by Ibn Zayd. The fifth is the prophets and the believers. This was said by al-Zajjaj. Ibn al-Anbari said: the benefit of informing the witnesses of what God knows is to magnify the matter witnessed against and to repel denial concerning it.

The second is that it is the Qur'an, so the meaning is: do not be in doubt that the Qur'an is from God, the Exalted. This was said by Muqatil. Ibn 'Abbas said: what is meant by "the people" here is the people of Makkah.

His saying, ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord﴾: Al-Zajjaj said: He mentioned their being presented in order to emphasize their state regarding retribution against them, even though others are also presented.

As for "the witnesses" (al-ashhad), there are five opinions regarding them: The first is that they are the messengers. This was said by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas. The second is the angels. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah. The third is the creatures; this was also narrated from Qatadah. Muqatil said: "al-ashhad" means the people, as one says "in the presence of the witnesses," meaning in the presence of the people. The fourth is the angels, the prophets, and the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), who bear witness over the people, and the limbs bear witness against the son of Adam. This was said by Ibn Zayd. The fifth is the prophets and the believers. This was said by al-Zajjaj. Ibn al-Anbari said: the benefit of informing the witnesses of what God knows is to magnify the matter witnessed against and to repel denial concerning it.

(p-90) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who bar [others] from the way of Allah﴾ — its explanation has already been given in (al-A'raf: 45).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they, in the Hereafter, they are disbelievers﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: "Hum" is mentioned a second time for emphasis, to affirm the extent of their disbelief.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verses 20–21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They were not able to escape [Allah] on the earth﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "They could not escape Me if I commanded the earth to swallow them up." ﴿And they had no protectors other than Allah﴾, meaning: they had no protector among those they worshipped who could prevent them from Me.

Ibn al-Anbari said: Since the custom of the Arabs was to say, "There is no refuge (wizr) for you from me, nor a tunnel (nafq)," by wizr they meant a mountain and by nafq a passage underground, and both are places to which the one who fears takes refuge, Allah, exalted is He, informed that these disbelievers cannot outrun Him in flight, nor find anything that could block between them and His punishment from all that conceals and provides refuge in the earth. He said: His saying ﴿protectors﴾ implies an omitted element, its paraphrase being: "protectors who would shield them from the punishment of Allah," and this was omitted because it is well known.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Their punishment will be doubled﴾, meaning the leaders who barred others from the way of Allah, because of their misguiding their followers and others imitating them.

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿They were not able to escape in the earth﴾ means in the abode of this world, and they had no protector to prevent them from the retribution of Allah. Then He began anew: "Their punishment will be doubled," because of the magnitude of their disbelief in His Prophet, in the Resurrection and in the gathering.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They were not able to hear﴾. Regarding who is meant by this, there are two views:

The first: they are the disbelievers. Then, concerning its meaning, there are three statements. One: they were unable to (p-91) hear good or see the truth or perform obedience, because Allah, exalted is He, placed a barrier between them and that. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil. The second: the meaning is: "Their punishment will be doubled for what they were able to hear but did not listen to, and for what they could see of the proofs of Allah but did not take heed of them," so the preposition (bi, "for") was dropped, as the Arabs say: "I will reward you for what you have done" (la-ajziyannaka ma ʿamilta), and "for what you have done" (bi-ma ʿamilta). This was mentioned by al-Farra', and Ibn al-Anbari cited as evidence for it the verse:

"We make the meat dear to the guests raw, and we give it away when the cooking-pots have boiled."

He intended: "we make dear with the meat." The third: because of the intensity of their disbelief and their enmity toward the Prophet ﷺ, they could not understand what he was saying. This was stated by al-Zajjaj.

The second view: they are the idols. The meaning then is: the deities had no hearing nor sight, so they were not able to hear, and they did not see. On this view, the phrase ﴿they were﴾ refers to their protectors, which are the idols. This meaning is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbas.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا جَرَمَ﴾ (Surely / Certainly). قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: يُرِيدُ: حَقًّا إنَّهُمُ الأخْسَرُونَ. وقالَ الفَرّاءُ: "لا جَرَمَ" كَلِمَةٌ كانَتْ في الأصْلِ بِمَنزِلَةِ "لا بُدَّ" و"لا مَحالَةَ"، فَجَرَتْ عَلى ذَلِكَ، وكَثُرَ اسْتِعْمالُهم إيّاها حَتّى صارَتْ بِمَنزِلَةِ "حَقًّا"، ألا تَرى أنَّ العَرَبَ تَقُولُ: لا جَرَمَ لَآتِيَنَّكَ، لا جَرَمَ لَقَدْ أحْسَنْتَ، وأصْلُها مِن "جَرَمْتُ"، أيْ: كَسَبْتُ الذَّنْبَ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: ومَعْنى "لا جَرَمَ": "لا" نَفْيٌ لِما ظَنُّوا أنَّهُ يَنْفَعُهم (p-٩٢) كَأنَّ المَعْنى: لا يَنْفَعُهم ذَلِكَ، جَرَمَ أنَّهم في الآخِرَةِ هُمُ الأخْسَرُونَ، أيْ: كَسَبَ لَهم ذَلِكَ الفِعْلُ الخُسْرانَ. وذَكَرَ ابْنُ الأنْبارِيِّ أنَّ "لا" رَدٌّ عَلى أهْلِ الكُفْرِ فِيما قَدَّرُوهُ مِنِ انْدِفاعِ الشَّرِّ عَنْهم في الآخِرَةِ، والمَعْنى: لا يَنْدَفِعُ عَنْهم عَذابِي، ولا يَجِدُونَ ولِيًّا يَصْرِفُ عَنْهم نِقْمَتِي، ثُمَّ ابْتَدَأ مُسْتَأْنِفًا "جَرَمَ"، قالَ: وفِيها قَوْلانِ:

أحَدُهُما: أنَّها بِمَعْنى: كَسَبَ، كَفْرُهم وما قَدَّرُوا مِنَ الباطِلِ وُقُوعَ العَذابِ بِهِمْ. فَـ"جَرَمَ" فِعْلٌ ماضٍ، مَعْناهُ: كَسَبَ، وفاعِلُهُ مُضْمَرٌ فِيهِ مِن ذِكْرِ الكُفْرِ وتَقْرِيرِ الباطِلِ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ مَعْنى جَرَمَ: أحَقَّ وصَحَّ، وهو فِعْلٌ ماضٍ، وفاعِلُهُ مُضْمَرٌ فِيهِ، والمَعْنى: أحَقَّ كُفْرُهم وُقُوعَ العَذابِ والخُسْرانِ بِهِمْ، قالَ الشّاعِرُ:

؎ ولَقَدْ طَعَنْتَ أبا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً جَرَمَتْ فَزارَةَ بَعْدَها أنْ يَغْضَبُوا

أرادَ: حَقَّتِ الطَّعْنَةُ فَزارَةَ بِالغَضَبِ. ومِنَ العَرَبِ مَن يُغَيِّرُ لَفْظَ "جَرَمَ" مَعَ "لا" خاصَّةً، فَيَقُولُ بَعْضُهم: "لا جُرْمَ"، ويَقُولُ آخَرُونَ: "لا جَرْ" بِإسْقاطِ المِيمِ، ويُقالُ: "لاذا جَرَمَ" و"لاذا جَرْ" بِغَيْرِ مِيمٍ، و"لا إنْ ذا جُرْمٌ" و"لا عَنْ ذا جُرْمٌ"، ومَعْنى اللُّغاتِ كُلِّها: حَقًّا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَأخْبَتُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ﴾ (And they humbled themselves before their Lord). فِيهِ سَبْعَةُ أقْوالٍ:

أحَدُها: خافُوا رَبَّهم، رَواهُ ابْنُ أبِي طَلْحَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. والثّانِي: أنابُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ، رَواهُ العَوْفِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. والثّالِثُ: ثابُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. (p-٩٣) والرّابِعُ: اطْمَأنُّوا، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ. والخامِسُ: أخْلَصُوا، قالَهُ مُقاتِلٌ. والسّادِسُ: تَخَشَّعُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ، قالَهُ الفَرّاءُ. والسّابِعُ: تَواضَعُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ، قالَهُ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: لِمَ أُوثِرَتْ "إلى" عَلى اللّامِ في قَوْلِهِ: "وأخْبَتُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ"، والعادَةُ جارِيَةٌ بِأنْ يُقالَ: أخْبَتُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ؟

فالجَوابُ: أنَّ المَعْنى: وجَّهُوا خَوْفَهم وخُشُوعَهم وإخْلاصَهم إلى رَبِّهِمْ، واطْمَأنُّوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ. قالَ الفَرّاءُ: ورُبَّما جَعَلَتِ العَرَبُ "إلى" في مَوْضِعِ اللّامِ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿بِأنَّ رَبَّكَ أوْحى لَها﴾ [الزِّلْزالِ: ٥] (because your Lord has inspired it)، وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿الَّذِي هَدانا لِهَذا﴾ [الأعْرافِ: ٤٣] (Who guided us to this). وقَدْ يَجُوزُ في العَرَبِيَّةِ: فُلانٌ يُخْبِتُ إلى اللَّهِ، يُرِيدُ: يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ مُوَجِّهًا وجْهَهُ إلى اللَّهِ. قالَ بَعْضُ المُفَسِّرِينَ: هَذِهِ الآيَةُ نازِلَةٌ في أصْحابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وما قَبْلَها نازِلٌ في المُشْرِكِينَ. ثُمَّ ضَرَبَ لِلْفَرِيقَيْنِ مَثَلًا، فَقالَ: ﴿مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ كالأعْمى والأصَمِّ﴾ (The likeness of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf). قالَ مُجاهِدٌ: الفَرِيقانِ المُؤْمِنُ والكافِرُ. فَأمّا الأعْمى والأصَمُّ فَهو الكافِرُ، وأمّا البَصِيرُ والسَّمِيعُ فَهو المُؤْمِنُ. قالَ قَتادَةُ: الكافِرُ عَمِيَ عَنِ الحَقِّ وصُمَّ عَنْهُ، والمُؤْمِنُ: أبْصَرَ الحَقَّ وسَمِعَهُ ثُمَّ انْتَفَعَ بِهِ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: في الكَلامِ ضَمِيرٌ، تَقْدِيرُهُ: مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ كَمَثَلِ الأعْمى. وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ المُسْلِمَيْنِ كالبَصِيرِ والسَّمِيعِ، ومَثَلُ فَرِيقِ الكافِرِينَ كالأعْمى والأصَمِّ، لِأنَّهم في عَداوَتِهِمْ وتَرْكِهِمْ لِلْفَهْمِ بِمَنزِلَةِ مَن يَسْمَعُ ولا يُبْصِرُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوِيانِ مَثَلًا﴾ (Are the two equal in likeness?) أيْ: هَلْ يَسْتَوِيانِ في المُشابَهَةِ؟

والمَعْنى: كَما لا يَسْتَوِيانِ عِنْدَكم، كَذَلِكَ لا يَسْتَوِي المُؤْمِنُ والكافِرُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: "هَلْ" هاهُنا بِمَعْنى الإيجابِ، لا بِمَعْنى الِاسْتِفْهامِ، والمَعْنى: لا يَسْتَوِيانِ. قالَ الفَرّاءُ: وإنَّما لَمْ يَقُلْ: "يَسْتَوُونَ" لِأنَّ الأعْمى والأصَمَّ مِن (p-٩٤) صِفَةِ واحِدٍ، والسَّمِيعَ والبَصِيرَ مِن صِفَةِ واحِدٍ، كَقَوْلِ القائِلِ: مَرَرْتُ بِالعاقِلِ واللَّبِيبِ، وهو يَعْنِي واحِدًا، قالَ الشّاعِرُ:

؎ وما أدْرِي إذا يَمَّمْتُ أرْضًا ∗∗∗ أُرِيدُ الخَيْرَ أيُّهُما يَلِينِي

فَقالَ: "أيُّهُما". وإنَّما ذَكَرَ الخَيْرَ وحْدَهُ، لِأنَّ المَعْنى يُعْرَفُ، إذِ المُبْتَغِي لِلْخَيْرِ مُتَّقٍ لِلشَّرِّ. وقالَ ابْنُ الأنْبارِيِّ: الأعْمى والأصَمُّ صِفَتانِ لِكافِرٍ، والسَّمِيعُ والبَصِيرُ صِفَتانِ لِمُؤْمِنٍ، فَرَدَّ الفِعْلَ إلى المَوْصُوفِينَ بِالأوْصافِ الأرْبَعَةِ، كَما تَقُولُ: العاقِلُ والعالِمُ، والظّالِمُ والجاهِلُ، حَضَرا مَجْلِسِي، فَتُثَنِّي الخَبَرَ بَعْدَ ذِكْرِكَ أرْبَعَةً، لِأنَّ المَوْصُوفَ بِالعِلْمِ هو المَوْصُوفُ بِالعَقْلِ، وكَذَلِكَ المَنعُوتُ بِالجَهْلِ هو المَنعُوتُ بِالظُّلْمِ، فَلَمّا كانَ المَنعُوتانِ اثْنَيْنِ، رَجَعَ الخَبَرُ إلَيْهِما، ولَمْ يُلْتَفَتْ إلى تَفْرِيقِ الأوْصافِ، ألا تَرى أنَّهُ يَسُوغُ أنْ تَقُولَ: الأدِيبُ واللَّبِيبُ والكَرِيمُ والجَمِيلُ قَصَدَنِي، فَتُوَحِّدُ الفِعْلَ بَعْدَ أوْصافٍ لِعِلَّةِ أنَّ المَوْصُوفَ بِهِنَّ واحِدٌ، ولا يَمْتَنِعُ عَطْفُ النُّعُوتِ عَلى النُّعُوتِ بِحُرُوفِ العَطْفِ، والمَوْصُوفُ واحِدٌ، فَقَدْ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿التّائِبُونَ العابِدُونَ﴾ [التَّوْبَةِ: ١١٢] (those who repent, who worship) ثُمَّ قالَ: "الآمِرُونَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ والنّاهُونَ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ" فَلَمْ يَقْتَضِ دُخُولُ الواوِ وُقُوعَ خِلافٍ بَيْنَ الآمِرِينَ والنّاهِينَ، وقَدْ قِيلَ: الآمِرُ بِالمَعْرُوفِ ناهٍ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ في حالِ أمْرِهِ، وكانَ دُخُولُ الواوِ دَلالَةً عَلى الآمِرِ بِالمَعْرُوفِ، لِأنَّ الأمْرَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ لا يَنْفَرِدُ دُونَ النَّهْيِ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ، كَما يَنْفَرِدُ الحامِدُونَ بِالحَمْدِ دُونَ السّائِحِينَ، والسّائِحُونَ بِالسِّياحَةِ دُونَ الحامِدِينَ، ويَدُلُّ أيْضًا عَلى أنَّ العَرَبَ تَنْسِقُ النَّعْتَ عَلى النَّعْتِ والمَنعُوتُ واحِدٌ، كَقَوْلِ الشّاعِرِ يُخاطِبُ سَعِيدَ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمانَ بْنِ عَفّانَ: (p-٩٥)

؎ يَظُنُّ سَعِيدٌ وابْنُ عَمْرٍو بِأنَّنِي ∗∗∗ إذا سامَنِي ذُلًّا أكُونُ بِهِ أرْضى

فَنَسَقَ ابْنَ عَمْرٍو عَلى سَعِيدٍ، وهو سَعِيدٌ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا جَرَمَ﴾ (Surely / Certainly). قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: يُرِيدُ: حَقًّا إنَّهُمُ الأخْسَرُونَ. وقالَ الفَرّاءُ: "لا جَرَمَ" كَلِمَةٌ كانَتْ في الأصْلِ بِمَنزِلَةِ "لا بُدَّ" و"لا مَحالَةَ"، فَجَرَتْ عَلى ذَلِكَ، وكَثُرَ اسْتِعْمالُهم إيّاها حَتّى صارَتْ بِمَنزِلَةِ "حَقًّا"، ألا تَرى أنَّ العَرَبَ تَقُولُ: لا جَرَمَ لَآتِيَنَّكَ، لا جَرَمَ لَقَدْ أحْسَنْتَ، وأصْلُها مِن "جَرَمْتُ"، أيْ: كَسَبْتُ الذَّنْبَ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: ومَعْنى "لا جَرَمَ": "لا" نَفْيٌ لِما ظَنُّوا أنَّهُ يَنْفَعُهم (p-٩٢) كَأنَّ المَعْنى: لا يَنْفَعُهم ذَلِكَ، جَرَمَ أنَّهم في الآخِرَةِ هُمُ الأخْسَرُونَ، أيْ: كَسَبَ لَهم ذَلِكَ الفِعْلُ الخُسْرانَ. وذَكَرَ ابْنُ الأنْبارِيِّ أنَّ "لا" رَدٌّ عَلى أهْلِ الكُفْرِ فِيما قَدَّرُوهُ مِنِ انْدِفاعِ الشَّرِّ عَنْهم في الآخِرَةِ، والمَعْنى: لا يَنْدَفِعُ عَنْهم عَذابِي، ولا يَجِدُونَ ولِيًّا يَصْرِفُ عَنْهم نِقْمَتِي، ثُمَّ ابْتَدَأ مُسْتَأْنِفًا "جَرَمَ"، قالَ: وفِيها قَوْلانِ:

أحَدُهُما: أنَّها بِمَعْنى: كَسَبَ، كَفْرُهم وما قَدَّرُوا مِنَ الباطِلِ وُقُوعَ العَذابِ بِهِمْ. فَـ"جَرَمَ" فِعْلٌ ماضٍ، مَعْناهُ: كَسَبَ، وفاعِلُهُ مُضْمَرٌ فِيهِ مِن ذِكْرِ الكُفْرِ وتَقْرِيرِ الباطِلِ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ مَعْنى جَرَمَ: أحَقَّ وصَحَّ، وهو فِعْلٌ ماضٍ، وفاعِلُهُ مُضْمَرٌ فِيهِ، والمَعْنى: أحَقَّ كُفْرُهم وُقُوعَ العَذابِ والخُسْرانِ بِهِمْ، قالَ الشّاعِرُ:

؎ ولَقَدْ طَعَنْتَ أبا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً جَرَمَتْ فَزارَةَ بَعْدَها أنْ يَغْضَبُوا

أرادَ: حَقَّتِ الطَّعْنَةُ فَزارَةَ بِالغَضَبِ. ومِنَ العَرَبِ مَن يُغَيِّرُ لَفْظَ "جَرَمَ" مَعَ "لا" خاصَّةً، فَيَقُولُ بَعْضُهم: "لا جُرْمَ"، ويَقُولُ آخَرُونَ: "لا جَرْ" بِإسْقاطِ المِيمِ، ويُقالُ: "لاذا جَرَمَ" و"لاذا جَرْ" بِغَيْرِ مِيمٍ، و"لا إنْ ذا جُرْمٌ" و"لا عَنْ ذا جُرْمٌ"، ومَعْنى اللُّغاتِ كُلِّها: حَقًّا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَأخْبَتُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ﴾ (And they humbled themselves before their Lord). فِيهِ سَبْعَةُ أقْوالٍ:

أحَدُها: خافُوا رَبَّهم، رَواهُ ابْنُ أبِي طَلْحَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. والثّانِي: أنابُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ، رَواهُ العَوْفِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. والثّالِثُ: ثابُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. (p-٩٣) والرّابِعُ: اطْمَأنُّوا، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ. والخامِسُ: أخْلَصُوا، قالَهُ مُقاتِلٌ. والسّادِسُ: تَخَشَّعُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ، قالَهُ الفَرّاءُ. والسّابِعُ: تَواضَعُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ، قالَهُ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: لِمَ أُوثِرَتْ "إلى" عَلى اللّامِ في قَوْلِهِ: "وأخْبَتُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ"، والعادَةُ جارِيَةٌ بِأنْ يُقالَ: أخْبَتُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ؟

فالجَوابُ: أنَّ المَعْنى: وجَّهُوا خَوْفَهم وخُشُوعَهم وإخْلاصَهم إلى رَبِّهِمْ، واطْمَأنُّوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ. قالَ الفَرّاءُ: ورُبَّما جَعَلَتِ العَرَبُ "إلى" في مَوْضِعِ اللّامِ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿بِأنَّ رَبَّكَ أوْحى لَها﴾ [الزِّلْزالِ: ٥] (because your Lord has inspired it)، وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿الَّذِي هَدانا لِهَذا﴾ [الأعْرافِ: ٤٣] (Who guided us to this). وقَدْ يَجُوزُ في العَرَبِيَّةِ: فُلانٌ يُخْبِتُ إلى اللَّهِ، يُرِيدُ: يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ مُوَجِّهًا وجْهَهُ إلى اللَّهِ. قالَ بَعْضُ المُفَسِّرِينَ: هَذِهِ الآيَةُ نازِلَةٌ في أصْحابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وما قَبْلَها نازِلٌ في المُشْرِكِينَ. ثُمَّ ضَرَبَ لِلْفَرِيقَيْنِ مَثَلًا، فَقالَ: ﴿مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ كالأعْمى والأصَمِّ﴾ (The likeness of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf). قالَ مُجاهِدٌ: الفَرِيقانِ المُؤْمِنُ والكافِرُ. فَأمّا الأعْمى والأصَمُّ فَهو الكافِرُ، وأمّا البَصِيرُ والسَّمِيعُ فَهو المُؤْمِنُ. قالَ قَتادَةُ: الكافِرُ عَمِيَ عَنِ الحَقِّ وصُمَّ عَنْهُ، والمُؤْمِنُ: أبْصَرَ الحَقَّ وسَمِعَهُ ثُمَّ انْتَفَعَ بِهِ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: في الكَلامِ ضَمِيرٌ، تَقْدِيرُهُ: مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ كَمَثَلِ الأعْمى. وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ المُسْلِمَيْنِ كالبَصِيرِ والسَّمِيعِ، ومَثَلُ فَرِيقِ الكافِرِينَ كالأعْمى والأصَمِّ، لِأنَّهم في عَداوَتِهِمْ وتَرْكِهِمْ لِلْفَهْمِ بِمَنزِلَةِ مَن يَسْمَعُ ولا يُبْصِرُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوِيانِ مَثَلًا﴾ (Are the two equal in likeness?) أيْ: هَلْ يَسْتَوِيانِ في المُشابَهَةِ؟

والمَعْنى: كَما لا يَسْتَوِيانِ عِنْدَكم، كَذَلِكَ لا يَسْتَوِي المُؤْمِنُ والكافِرُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: "هَلْ" هاهُنا بِمَعْنى الإيجابِ، لا بِمَعْنى الِاسْتِفْهامِ، والمَعْنى: لا يَسْتَوِيانِ. قالَ الفَرّاءُ: وإنَّما لَمْ يَقُلْ: "يَسْتَوُونَ" لِأنَّ الأعْمى والأصَمَّ مِن (p-٩٤) صِفَةِ واحِدٍ، والسَّمِيعَ والبَصِيرَ مِن صِفَةِ واحِدٍ، كَقَوْلِ القائِلِ: مَرَرْتُ بِالعاقِلِ واللَّبِيبِ، وهو يَعْنِي واحِدًا، قالَ الشّاعِرُ:

؎ وما أدْرِي إذا يَمَّمْتُ أرْضًا ∗∗∗ أُرِيدُ الخَيْرَ أيُّهُما يَلِينِي

فَقالَ: "أيُّهُما". وإنَّما ذَكَرَ الخَيْرَ وحْدَهُ، لِأنَّ المَعْنى يُعْرَفُ، إذِ المُبْتَغِي لِلْخَيْرِ مُتَّقٍ لِلشَّرِّ. وقالَ ابْنُ الأنْبارِيِّ: الأعْمى والأصَمُّ صِفَتانِ لِكافِرٍ، والسَّمِيعُ والبَصِيرُ صِفَتانِ لِمُؤْمِنٍ، فَرَدَّ الفِعْلَ إلى المَوْصُوفِينَ بِالأوْصافِ الأرْبَعَةِ، كَما تَقُولُ: العاقِلُ والعالِمُ، والظّالِمُ والجاهِلُ، حَضَرا مَجْلِسِي، فَتُثَنِّي الخَبَرَ بَعْدَ ذِكْرِكَ أرْبَعَةً، لِأنَّ المَوْصُوفَ بِالعِلْمِ هو المَوْصُوفُ بِالعَقْلِ، وكَذَلِكَ المَنعُوتُ بِالجَهْلِ هو المَنعُوتُ بِالظُّلْمِ، فَلَمّا كانَ المَنعُوتانِ اثْنَيْنِ، رَجَعَ الخَبَرُ إلَيْهِما، ولَمْ يُلْتَفَتْ إلى تَفْرِيقِ الأوْصافِ، ألا تَرى أنَّهُ يَسُوغُ أنْ تَقُولَ: الأدِيبُ واللَّبِيبُ والكَرِيمُ والجَمِيلُ قَصَدَنِي، فَتُوَحِّدُ الفِعْلَ بَعْدَ أوْصافٍ لِعِلَّةِ أنَّ المَوْصُوفَ بِهِنَّ واحِدٌ، ولا يَمْتَنِعُ عَطْفُ النُّعُوتِ عَلى النُّعُوتِ بِحُرُوفِ العَطْفِ، والمَوْصُوفُ واحِدٌ، فَقَدْ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿التّائِبُونَ العابِدُونَ﴾ [التَّوْبَةِ: ١١٢] (those who repent, who worship) ثُمَّ قالَ: "الآمِرُونَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ والنّاهُونَ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ" فَلَمْ يَقْتَضِ دُخُولُ الواوِ وُقُوعَ خِلافٍ بَيْنَ الآمِرِينَ والنّاهِينَ، وقَدْ قِيلَ: الآمِرُ بِالمَعْرُوفِ ناهٍ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ في حالِ أمْرِهِ، وكانَ دُخُولُ الواوِ دَلالَةً عَلى الآمِرِ بِالمَعْرُوفِ، لِأنَّ الأمْرَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ لا يَنْفَرِدُ دُونَ النَّهْيِ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ، كَما يَنْفَرِدُ الحامِدُونَ بِالحَمْدِ دُونَ السّائِحِينَ، والسّائِحُونَ بِالسِّياحَةِ دُونَ الحامِدِينَ، ويَدُلُّ أيْضًا عَلى أنَّ العَرَبَ تَنْسِقُ النَّعْتَ عَلى النَّعْتِ والمَنعُوتُ واحِدٌ، كَقَوْلِ الشّاعِرِ يُخاطِبُ سَعِيدَ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمانَ بْنِ عَفّانَ: (p-٩٥)

؎ يَظُنُّ سَعِيدٌ وابْنُ عَمْرٍو بِأنَّنِي ∗∗∗ إذا سامَنِي ذُلًّا أكُونُ بِهِ أرْضى

فَنَسَقَ ابْنَ عَمْرٍو عَلى سَعِيدٍ، وهو سَعِيدٌ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا جَرَمَ﴾ (Surely / Certainly). قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: يُرِيدُ: حَقًّا إنَّهُمُ الأخْسَرُونَ. وقالَ الفَرّاءُ: "لا جَرَمَ" كَلِمَةٌ كانَتْ في الأصْلِ بِمَنزِلَةِ "لا بُدَّ" و"لا مَحالَةَ"، فَجَرَتْ عَلى ذَلِكَ، وكَثُرَ اسْتِعْمالُهم إيّاها حَتّى صارَتْ بِمَنزِلَةِ "حَقًّا"، ألا تَرى أنَّ العَرَبَ تَقُولُ: لا جَرَمَ لَآتِيَنَّكَ، لا جَرَمَ لَقَدْ أحْسَنْتَ، وأصْلُها مِن "جَرَمْتُ"، أيْ: كَسَبْتُ الذَّنْبَ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: ومَعْنى "لا جَرَمَ": "لا" نَفْيٌ لِما ظَنُّوا أنَّهُ يَنْفَعُهم (p-٩٢) كَأنَّ المَعْنى: لا يَنْفَعُهم ذَلِكَ، جَرَمَ أنَّهم في الآخِرَةِ هُمُ الأخْسَرُونَ، أيْ: كَسَبَ لَهم ذَلِكَ الفِعْلُ الخُسْرانَ. وذَكَرَ ابْنُ الأنْبارِيِّ أنَّ "لا" رَدٌّ عَلى أهْلِ الكُفْرِ فِيما قَدَّرُوهُ مِنِ انْدِفاعِ الشَّرِّ عَنْهم في الآخِرَةِ، والمَعْنى: لا يَنْدَفِعُ عَنْهم عَذابِي، ولا يَجِدُونَ ولِيًّا يَصْرِفُ عَنْهم نِقْمَتِي، ثُمَّ ابْتَدَأ مُسْتَأْنِفًا "جَرَمَ"، قالَ: وفِيها قَوْلانِ:

أحَدُهُما: أنَّها بِمَعْنى: كَسَبَ، كَفْرُهم وما قَدَّرُوا مِنَ الباطِلِ وُقُوعَ العَذابِ بِهِمْ. فَـ"جَرَمَ" فِعْلٌ ماضٍ، مَعْناهُ: كَسَبَ، وفاعِلُهُ مُضْمَرٌ فِيهِ مِن ذِكْرِ الكُفْرِ وتَقْرِيرِ الباطِلِ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ مَعْنى جَرَمَ: أحَقَّ وصَحَّ، وهو فِعْلٌ ماضٍ، وفاعِلُهُ مُضْمَرٌ فِيهِ، والمَعْنى: أحَقَّ كُفْرُهم وُقُوعَ العَذابِ والخُسْرانِ بِهِمْ، قالَ الشّاعِرُ:

؎ ولَقَدْ طَعَنْتَ أبا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً جَرَمَتْ فَزارَةَ بَعْدَها أنْ يَغْضَبُوا

أرادَ: حَقَّتِ الطَّعْنَةُ فَزارَةَ بِالغَضَبِ. ومِنَ العَرَبِ مَن يُغَيِّرُ لَفْظَ "جَرَمَ" مَعَ "لا" خاصَّةً، فَيَقُولُ بَعْضُهم: "لا جُرْمَ"، ويَقُولُ آخَرُونَ: "لا جَرْ" بِإسْقاطِ المِيمِ، ويُقالُ: "لاذا جَرَمَ" و"لاذا جَرْ" بِغَيْرِ مِيمٍ، و"لا إنْ ذا جُرْمٌ" و"لا عَنْ ذا جُرْمٌ"، ومَعْنى اللُّغاتِ كُلِّها: حَقًّا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَأخْبَتُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ﴾ (And they humbled themselves before their Lord). فِيهِ سَبْعَةُ أقْوالٍ:

أحَدُها: خافُوا رَبَّهم، رَواهُ ابْنُ أبِي طَلْحَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. والثّانِي: أنابُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ، رَواهُ العَوْفِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. والثّالِثُ: ثابُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. (p-٩٣) والرّابِعُ: اطْمَأنُّوا، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ. والخامِسُ: أخْلَصُوا، قالَهُ مُقاتِلٌ. والسّادِسُ: تَخَشَّعُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ، قالَهُ الفَرّاءُ. والسّابِعُ: تَواضَعُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ، قالَهُ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: لِمَ أُوثِرَتْ "إلى" عَلى اللّامِ في قَوْلِهِ: "وأخْبَتُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ"، والعادَةُ جارِيَةٌ بِأنْ يُقالَ: أخْبَتُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ؟

فالجَوابُ: أنَّ المَعْنى: وجَّهُوا خَوْفَهم وخُشُوعَهم وإخْلاصَهم إلى رَبِّهِمْ، واطْمَأنُّوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ. قالَ الفَرّاءُ: ورُبَّما جَعَلَتِ العَرَبُ "إلى" في مَوْضِعِ اللّامِ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿بِأنَّ رَبَّكَ أوْحى لَها﴾ [الزِّلْزالِ: ٥] (because your Lord has inspired it)، وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿الَّذِي هَدانا لِهَذا﴾ [الأعْرافِ: ٤٣] (Who guided us to this). وقَدْ يَجُوزُ في العَرَبِيَّةِ: فُلانٌ يُخْبِتُ إلى اللَّهِ، يُرِيدُ: يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ مُوَجِّهًا وجْهَهُ إلى اللَّهِ. قالَ بَعْضُ المُفَسِّرِينَ: هَذِهِ الآيَةُ نازِلَةٌ في أصْحابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وما قَبْلَها نازِلٌ في المُشْرِكِينَ. ثُمَّ ضَرَبَ لِلْفَرِيقَيْنِ مَثَلًا، فَقالَ: ﴿مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ كالأعْمى والأصَمِّ﴾ (The likeness of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf). قالَ مُجاهِدٌ: الفَرِيقانِ المُؤْمِنُ والكافِرُ. فَأمّا الأعْمى والأصَمُّ فَهو الكافِرُ، وأمّا البَصِيرُ والسَّمِيعُ فَهو المُؤْمِنُ. قالَ قَتادَةُ: الكافِرُ عَمِيَ عَنِ الحَقِّ وصُمَّ عَنْهُ، والمُؤْمِنُ: أبْصَرَ الحَقَّ وسَمِعَهُ ثُمَّ انْتَفَعَ بِهِ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: في الكَلامِ ضَمِيرٌ، تَقْدِيرُهُ: مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ كَمَثَلِ الأعْمى. وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ المُسْلِمَيْنِ كالبَصِيرِ والسَّمِيعِ، ومَثَلُ فَرِيقِ الكافِرِينَ كالأعْمى والأصَمِّ، لِأنَّهم في عَداوَتِهِمْ وتَرْكِهِمْ لِلْفَهْمِ بِمَنزِلَةِ مَن يَسْمَعُ ولا يُبْصِرُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوِيانِ مَثَلًا﴾ (Are the two equal in likeness?) أيْ: هَلْ يَسْتَوِيانِ في المُشابَهَةِ؟

والمَعْنى: كَما لا يَسْتَوِيانِ عِنْدَكم، كَذَلِكَ لا يَسْتَوِي المُؤْمِنُ والكافِرُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: "هَلْ" هاهُنا بِمَعْنى الإيجابِ، لا بِمَعْنى الِاسْتِفْهامِ، والمَعْنى: لا يَسْتَوِيانِ. قالَ الفَرّاءُ: وإنَّما لَمْ يَقُلْ: "يَسْتَوُونَ" لِأنَّ الأعْمى والأصَمَّ مِن (p-٩٤) صِفَةِ واحِدٍ، والسَّمِيعَ والبَصِيرَ مِن صِفَةِ واحِدٍ، كَقَوْلِ القائِلِ: مَرَرْتُ بِالعاقِلِ واللَّبِيبِ، وهو يَعْنِي واحِدًا، قالَ الشّاعِرُ:

؎ وما أدْرِي إذا يَمَّمْتُ أرْضًا ∗∗∗ أُرِيدُ الخَيْرَ أيُّهُما يَلِينِي

فَقالَ: "أيُّهُما". وإنَّما ذَكَرَ الخَيْرَ وحْدَهُ، لِأنَّ المَعْنى يُعْرَفُ، إذِ المُبْتَغِي لِلْخَيْرِ مُتَّقٍ لِلشَّرِّ. وقالَ ابْنُ الأنْبارِيِّ: الأعْمى والأصَمُّ صِفَتانِ لِكافِرٍ، والسَّمِيعُ والبَصِيرُ صِفَتانِ لِمُؤْمِنٍ، فَرَدَّ الفِعْلَ إلى المَوْصُوفِينَ بِالأوْصافِ الأرْبَعَةِ، كَما تَقُولُ: العاقِلُ والعالِمُ، والظّالِمُ والجاهِلُ، حَضَرا مَجْلِسِي، فَتُثَنِّي الخَبَرَ بَعْدَ ذِكْرِكَ أرْبَعَةً، لِأنَّ المَوْصُوفَ بِالعِلْمِ هو المَوْصُوفُ بِالعَقْلِ، وكَذَلِكَ المَنعُوتُ بِالجَهْلِ هو المَنعُوتُ بِالظُّلْمِ، فَلَمّا كانَ المَنعُوتانِ اثْنَيْنِ، رَجَعَ الخَبَرُ إلَيْهِما، ولَمْ يُلْتَفَتْ إلى تَفْرِيقِ الأوْصافِ، ألا تَرى أنَّهُ يَسُوغُ أنْ تَقُولَ: الأدِيبُ واللَّبِيبُ والكَرِيمُ والجَمِيلُ قَصَدَنِي، فَتُوَحِّدُ الفِعْلَ بَعْدَ أوْصافٍ لِعِلَّةِ أنَّ المَوْصُوفَ بِهِنَّ واحِدٌ، ولا يَمْتَنِعُ عَطْفُ النُّعُوتِ عَلى النُّعُوتِ بِحُرُوفِ العَطْفِ، والمَوْصُوفُ واحِدٌ، فَقَدْ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿التّائِبُونَ العابِدُونَ﴾ [التَّوْبَةِ: ١١٢] (those who repent, who worship) ثُمَّ قالَ: "الآمِرُونَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ والنّاهُونَ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ" فَلَمْ يَقْتَضِ دُخُولُ الواوِ وُقُوعَ خِلافٍ بَيْنَ الآمِرِينَ والنّاهِينَ، وقَدْ قِيلَ: الآمِرُ بِالمَعْرُوفِ ناهٍ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ في حالِ أمْرِهِ، وكانَ دُخُولُ الواوِ دَلالَةً عَلى الآمِرِ بِالمَعْرُوفِ، لِأنَّ الأمْرَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ لا يَنْفَرِدُ دُونَ النَّهْيِ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ، كَما يَنْفَرِدُ الحامِدُونَ بِالحَمْدِ دُونَ السّائِحِينَ، والسّائِحُونَ بِالسِّياحَةِ دُونَ الحامِدِينَ، ويَدُلُّ أيْضًا عَلى أنَّ العَرَبَ تَنْسِقُ النَّعْتَ عَلى النَّعْتِ والمَنعُوتُ واحِدٌ، كَقَوْلِ الشّاعِرِ يُخاطِبُ سَعِيدَ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمانَ بْنِ عَفّانَ: (p-٩٥)

؎ يَظُنُّ سَعِيدٌ وابْنُ عَمْرٍو بِأنَّنِي ∗∗∗ إذا سامَنِي ذُلًّا أكُونُ بِهِ أرْضى

فَنَسَقَ ابْنَ عَمْرٍو عَلى سَعِيدٍ، وهو سَعِيدٌ.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verse 25–29:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed, I am﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and al-Kisa'i read "anni" with a fatha on the alif, the implied construction being: We sent him with (the message) that "I am to them a warner." The sense is that it is "that he is to them a warner," but it is in the shift from reporting about an absent party to addressing Noah's people directly. Nafi', 'Asim, Ibn 'Amir, and Hamzah read "inni" with a kasra on the alif, so it is taken as governed by an implied saying, the construction being: so he said to them, "Indeed, I am to you a warner."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We see you only as a human being like ourselves﴾. That is, a man like us, with no superiority for you over us. As for "al-arahil" (the lowly ones), Ibn 'Abbas said: they are the base people. Ibn Qutaybah said: they are the plural of "arhal," and it is said: a man is "rathl," and he has become "rathalah" and "ruthulah" (base). The meaning of "al-arahil" is: the wicked.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿At first sight﴾. Most readers read "badi" without a hamzah. Abu 'Amr read it with a hamzah after the dal. All of them hamzah "al-ra'y" except Abu 'Amr. Concerning the meaning of "badi" when it is not hamzated, the scholars have three views:

The first: the meaning is: "We do not see your followers except as our base and lowly ones at first sight, to every observer," meaning that the deficiency we have described them with is not hidden from anyone so that he would disagree with us. This is the view of Muqatil, among others.

The second: the meaning is that these people followed you in what appears outwardly from them, while their inner state is contrary to yours.

The third: the meaning is that they followed you in the outward appearance of their opinion, and did not reflect upon what you said; had they returned to reflection, they would not have followed you. Al-Zajjaj mentioned these two views. Ibn al-Anbari said: these three views are upon the reading of one who does not hamzate, since it comes from "bada, yabdu," meaning: it became apparent. As for one who hamzates "badi'," its meaning is: the beginning of opinion, i.e., they followed you at the first thing they began to consider, and had they reflected, they would not have turned away from agreeing with us in denying you.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And we do not see for you over us any superiority﴾. In it there are three views:

The first: superiority in creation, said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: in dominion, wealth, and the like, said by Muqatil. The third: that you have not been given preference by following Noah, and by opposing us in a virtue that we would follow you in seeking it; mentioned by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Rather, we think you are liars﴾. In it there are two views:

One: we are certain of you, said by al-Kalbi. The second: we suppose you, said by Muqatil.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾. That is, upon certainty and insight. Ibn al-Anbari said: his saying "in kuntu" (if I am) is a condition that does not imply any doubt attaching to him, but doubt attaches to those addressed among the people of deviation, so its implied meaning is: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord in your view. ﴿And He has given me mercy from Himself﴾. In it there are two views:

One: that it is prophethood, said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: guidance, said by Muqatil.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But it has been obscured from you﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, and Abu Bakr from 'Asim read "fa-amiyat" with a lightened mim and a fatha on the ayn. Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning is "you became blind to it"; it is said "amiya 'alayya hadha al-amr" when I did not understand it, and "amītu 'anhu" has the same meaning. al-Farra' said: this is among the things the Arabs have shifted the verb to, though in origin it belongs to something else, as in their saying: "the ring entered my hand," and "the shoe entered my foot," whereas it is the finger that enters the ring and the foot that enters the shoe; they permitted this because the meaning is well known. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from 'Asim read "fa-ʻummiyat" with a damma on the ayn and a shadda on the mim. Ibn al-Anbari said: the meaning of that is: Allah obscured it for you, since you were among those decreed to wretchedness. Likewise Ubayy ibn Ka'b and al-A'mash read: "fa-ʻammaha 'alaykum."

Concerning the referent of "it," there are two views: one: the clear evidence; the second: the mercy.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Shall we compel you to it﴾. That is: shall we compel you to accept it? This is an interrogative whose meaning is denial, as if he said: we are not able to compel you from our own selves. Qatadah said: By Allah, if the Prophet of Allah ﷺ had been able, he would have compelled it upon his people, but he did not possess that. It was said: Noah's intent (peace be upon him) was to refute their saying: ﴿and we do not see for you over us any superiority﴾, so he clarified his superiority and the superiority of those who believed in him, that he was upon clear evidence from his Lord, and that He had given him mercy from Himself, while the deniers were deprived of that.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿I do not ask you for any wealth for it﴾. That is, for my counsel and my calling you to it, ﴿wealth﴾, so that you might accuse me. Ibn al-Anbari said: since "mercy" carries the meaning of guidance and faith, it was permissible to make its verb masculine.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And I am not one to drive away those who have believed﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: they asked him to drive them away out of disdain, and he said: it is not permissible for me to drive them away, since they will meet Allah, and He will reward them for their faith, and will take for them from those who wronged them, and will diminish the affairs of those (who wronged them).

In his saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾, there are two views:

One: you are ignorant that this matter is from Allah, Exalted is He, said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: you are ignorant in your command to me to drive away the believers, said by Abu Sulayman.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verse 30–34:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And O my people, who would help me against Allah if I drove them away?﴾ That is: who would protect me from the punishment of Allah if I drove them away?

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor do I say to you, "With me are the treasuries of Allah"﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: By the "treasuries" he meant the knowledge of the unseen that is hidden from creation, because they had said to him: "These only follow you outwardly, and they are not with you [inwardly]." So he said to them: "I do not have the treasuries of Allah's hidden things, so as to know what the hearts conceal." The unseen matters were called "treasuries" because of their obscurity from people and their being concealed from them. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: The verses of the Qur'an are indeed treasuries; when you enter a treasury, strive not to leave it until you know what is in it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾. It was said: he said this to them because their land had become barren, and they asked him: "When will the rain come?" It was also said: rather, they asked him: "When will the punishment come?" So he said: "Nor do I know the unseen." And his saying: "Nor do I say that I am an angel" is a reply to their saying: ﴿We see you only as a human like ourselves﴾ [Hud: 27]. ﴿Nor do I say to those whom your eyes despise﴾, that is: whom you look down upon and consider insignificant, the believers. Al-Zajjaj said: "tazdari" means to deem little and despise; it is said: "zaraytu 'ala al-rajul" when you find fault with a man and belittle his deed, and "azraytu bihi" when you disparage him. The original form of "tazdari" is "tazturi," but this "ta'" is changed into "dal" after the "za'," because the "ta'" is one of the whispered letters, and whispered letters are soft, so the "ta'" after the "za'" would be concealed; so the "dal," being voiced, is substituted for it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah will not grant them any good﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: [i.e.] faith. The meaning of the speech is: it is not for me to look into what is in their souls and pass judgment upon them regarding anything, and their being despised by you does not nullify their reward. ﴿Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers﴾ if I said what has been mentioned before; and it was said: if I drove them away.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You have disputed with us﴾. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not be distressed﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: do not grieve. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: do not be humbled (la tastakin) and do not grieve. Abu Salih related from Ibn 'Abbas: "So do not grieve when the drowning befalls them" ﴿for what they used to do﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 11, verses 37–38:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And make the ark﴾, meaning: and build the ship.

Regarding His saying ﴿under Our eyes﴾ there are three opinions:

The first: in Our sight. This was said by Ibn Abbas. The second: under Our protection. This was said by al-Rabi'. The third: with Our knowledge. This was said by Muqatil. Ibn al-Anbari said: Indeed, He used the plural in accordance with the Arabic manner of using the plural for the singular. You say: "We went out to Basra in the ships," and He used the plural because it is the custom of a king to say: "We have commanded and We have forbidden."

Regarding His saying ﴿and Our revelation﴾ there are two opinions:

One: and Our command to you to make it. The second: and by Our teaching you how to make it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

One: Do not ask Me to pardon them. The second: Do not intercede with Me regarding their being given respite. He was forbidden from addressing Him about this in order to protect him from a request that would not be granted.

Indication of the manner of building the ship

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: Nuh was beaten, then wrapped in a felt cloak and thrown into his house. People thought he had died, then he would come out and call them. Until, when he despaired of his people's faith, a man came to him with his son, and he was leaning on a staff. The man said: "O my son, look at this old man, let him not deceive you." The son said: "O father, let me have the staff." So he took it and struck him a blow that caused a head wound (p-102) exposing the bone, and blood flowed over his face. He said: "My Lord, You see what Your servants do to me. If You have any need of them, then guide them; otherwise, grant me patience until You judge." So Allah revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾, up to His saying ﴿And make the ark﴾. He said: "My Lord, what is the ark?" He said: "A house of wood that runs upon the surface of the water, in which I will save the people of My obedience, and drown the people of My disobedience." He said: "My Lord, and where is the water?" He said: "Indeed, I am over whatever I will, Competent." He said: "My Lord, and where is the wood?" He said: "Plant the trees." So he planted teak trees for twenty years, and he refrained from calling them, and they refrained from him, except that they mocked him. When the trees matured, his Lord commanded him, and he cut them, dried them and joined them together. He said: "My Lord, how should I make this house?" He said: "Make it in three forms: its head like the head of a peacock, its breast like the breast of a bird, and its tail like the tail of a rooster. And make it closed." Allah sent Jibril to him to teach him, and revealed to him that he should hasten the work on the ship, for My anger has intensified against those who disobey Me. So he hired carpenters who worked with him, and Sam, Ham and Japheth were with him, carving the ship. He made its length six hundred cubits, its width three hundred and thirty cubits, and its height thirty-three. Allah caused a spring of pitch to gush for him, boiling vigorously until he coated it.

Also from Ibn Abbas, who said: He made three decks for it. In the lowest deck he carried the wild animals, predators and creeping things; in the middle, the beasts and livestock; and he and those with him rode in the uppermost deck.

It is narrated from al-Hasan that he said: The ship of Nuh was one thousand and two hundred cubits long, and its width was six hundred cubits.

Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that its length was three hundred cubits, its width five hundred cubits, and its height in the sky was thirty cubits.

Ibn Jurayj said: Its length was three hundred cubits, its width one hundred and fifty cubits, and its height in the sky was thirty cubits. At its top were the birds, in its middle were the people, and at its bottom were the predators.

Muqatil claimed that he built the ship over four hundred years.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whenever a group of his people passed by him, they mocked him﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

One: They saw him building the ship, and they had never seen a ship before, so they mocked and said: "After prophethood you have become a carpenter." This is the saying of Ibn Ishaq.

The second: They said to him: "What are you doing?" He said: "I am building a house that will walk upon the water," so they mocked his saying. This is the saying of Muqatil.

Regarding His saying ﴿If you mock us, then indeed we mock you﴾ there are five opinions:

One: If you mock our statement, then we mock your heedlessness.

The second: If you mock our action during the building of the ship, then we will mock you at the time of drowning. This was mentioned by the exegetes.

The third: If you mock us in this world, then we will mock you in the Hereafter. This was said by Ibn Jarir.

The fourth: If you consider us ignorant, then we consider you ignorant. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

The fifth: If you mock us, then we seek Allah's help against you. He called this mockery so that the two expressions would correspond, as we explained regarding His saying ﴿Allah mocks them﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:15]. This is the saying of Ibn al-Anbari.

Ibn Abbas said: Before the Flood there was neither river nor sea on earth, which is why they mocked him. The waters of the seas are only a remnant of the Flood.
